text: A dog has never eaten an orange in its life, and has never had scurvy. Neither has a cat, a cow, or a rat. They make their own vitamin C, in the liver, from sugar.

The assembly line runs four steps. You have the first three. The fourth enzyme is built by a gene called goo-lo. And in humans it isn't switched off. It's wrecked. A pile of broken fragments that hasn't made a working protein in tens of millions of years.
Not most people. Every human being alive. Every chimpanzee, gorilla and orangutan too. Whatever happened, happened to an ancestor we all share.

And the bill for this one is not subtle. Take away fresh food, and a human starts to fall apart. Bleeding gums, wounds reopening, old scars coming undone. Scurvy killed sailors on a scale that reshaped how navies planned voyages.
So was it an upgrade at all? Maybe not. Our ancestors may simply have eaten enough fruit that losing the factory cost very little. And a gene that costs nothing is a gene evolution stops maintaining.
Which makes this one different. Not a trade. A loss we got away with, right up until we got on boats.
We all lost that one. We all lost the next one too. And this time, you can feel it with your fingers.
